meta.name: A+ Academy — Aurora
references: https://www.apple.com/education/ (headless capture blank; type, spacing and surface rules from the known Apple system)
meta.audience: Arabic-first (RTL) secondary students, parents and teachers across the GCC and Egypt
meta.notes: Stripe gives the aurora gradient ribbon, indigo CTA and navy ink; Apple gives the restraint: huge quiet headlines, alternating light surfaces, generous whitespace, one idea per section.

primary.usage: Primary actions, links, focus. White text 5.4:1.

secondary.usage: Ink: headings and body text, dark sections.

accent.usage: Earned things only: discounts, streaks, what a student achieved. Never body text on white.

aurora.usage: The ribbon/mesh behind heroes and the intro; never behind body text.

neutral.usage: #0C1B33 is the foreground on light surfaces; #5F6B82 secondary text (5.3:1).

typography.rationale: One humanist family with Arabic and Latin drawn together, the Apple move: let size and weight do the work.

spacing.rhythm: 8-step multiples; sections separated by space, not rules

layout.alignment: start-aligned headlines (right in Arabic), centered only for the final CTA

shape.borders: 1px hairline #E4E7EF on cards; no heavy rules

iconography.landmarks: existing country landmark line icons kept

motion.principle: Marketing pages reveal on scroll; app pages only fade state changes; reduced motion removes all movement.

components.button_primary: pill, #5B4DFF fill, white 600 text, 44px min height, hover lifts 1px with a stronger shadow
components.button_secondary: pill, white fill, 1px hairline, ink text
components.card: white, 22px radius, hairline + card shadow, 24–32px padding
components.nav: translucent white with backdrop blur, hairline bottom, sticky
components.stat_tile: large tabular figure, small muted label, no chart junk

aesthetic.personality: a top school with a design studio: serious about results, warm to students

visual_language.contrast: high type contrast on near-white; colour only in the aurora and actions
visual_language.ornamentation: minimal; the aurora is the one ornament
visual_language.texture: smooth gradients, soft glass on the nav only

composition.strategy: one idea per section, big headline + supporting line + proof
composition.rhythm: alternate white and #F5F6FA sections; bento grids for features

imagery.style: real UI (course cards, dashboards) rendered as product shots; country flags and landmarks; teacher photos when they exist
imagery.never: stock smiles, invented testimonials or numbers

interaction_feel.feedback: subtle lift on hover, press scale .98
interaction_feel.scroll: content rises 16px and fades in once

overview.effect_intensity: medium on marketing, none in app
overview.performance_tier: mid: three.js on the home hero and intro only, poster image on phones and reduced motion

background_effects.type: aurora gradient ribbon / mesh (CSS conic + radial gradients, slow 20s drift)
background_effects.where: home hero, course catalogue header, final CTA

particle_systems.type: points on a sphere (three.js) forming the globe surface

3d_elements.type: glass-dot globe with GCC + Egypt pins in country colours and arcs between them
3d_elements.interaction: slow auto-rotate, pointer parallax, pauses off-screen

parallax.notes: hero globe drifts up slower than text

scroll_triggered_animations.notes: fade + 16px rise, once, via animation-timeline: view() with IntersectionObserver fallback

text_effects.type: gradient-clipped key word in the hero headline (aurora stops)

image_effects.type: product-shot cards tilt 2–4° in perspective in the hero bento

glassmorphism_neumorphism.type: nav bar and intro skip button only: white 72% + blur(16px)

svg_animations.type: A+ mark stroke-draw at the end of the intro

visual_effects.composite_notes: Intro (≈2.6s, once per tab session): aurora fades up → points fly in and assemble the globe → country pins light up one by one with arcs → camera dollies in → A+ wordmark resolves → overlay dissolves into the hero, where the same globe keeps turning. Skippable on any input.
